overview: The council approved loan orders for the Winthrop Street drainage project and a DPW facility and explored the adoption of meeting management software to increase public transparency. The body also referred an outdoor dining ordinance amendment to subcommittee and addressed various licensing and zoning matters.

items.title: Ceremonial Recognitions and Commendations
items.summary: Awarded certificates of appreciation and commendations to Chad Murphy and Associates for veteran housing repairs, George Turot for business leadership, State Representative Paul Donato as Democrat of the Year, and Pat Thurbridge as Citizen of the Year.

items.title: Amendment to Outdoor Dining License Ordinance
items.summary: Referred a proposed amendment to the Outdoor Dining License ordinance to the Zoning and Ordinance Subcommittee to clarify that council approval is required for city-owned property but not for private property. City Solicitor Mark Rumley explained the change would streamline the approval process for businesses.

items.title: Loan Order for Winthrop Street Drainage Project
items.summary: Approved a $350,000 loan order to cover cost overruns on the Winthrop Street drainage project caused by inaccurate engineering plans regarding subsurface rock and utility banks. Officials noted the city is seeking to recoup these costs through mediation with the engineering firm.

items.title: Loan Order for DPW Facility Project
items.summary: Passed a first reading for a $300,000 loan order to address underestimated soil contamination removal costs at the DPW facility site. The City Solicitor advised that recovery of these funds from the consultant was unlikely as the city would have incurred the removal costs regardless of the estimate accuracy.

items.title: Withdrawal of Hegner Center Deed Restrictions
items.summary: Noted the withdrawal of the Mayor's request regarding deed restrictions at 15 Maple Park Avenue, the site of the former Hegner Center.

items.title: License Approvals
items.summary: Approved a common victualer's license for Salvatore’s at 55 High Street and a taxi cab operator's license for Ezekiel Luzama. Councilor Marks recorded his opposition to the taxi license based on a standing request to update the taxi ordinance.

items.title: Meeting Management Technology and Transparency
items.summary: Approved a resolution to meet with vendors to explore software options for streamlining agenda posting, digital document access, and live-streaming of board and commission meetings. Councilors and members of the public spoke in favor of making municipal government more accessible and searchable through modern technology.

items.title: Truck Removal and Infrastructure Requests
items.summary: Approved requests to contact state police regarding abandoned trucks on Route 16 and for the developer of the Panera property to fulfill commitments regarding sidewalk repairs and crosswalk painting on Riverside Avenue.

items.title: Review of Off-Street Parking Zoning
items.summary: Approved a request for the Building Commission to provide recommendations for amending zoning ordinances to potentially allow more off-street parking in residential yards to alleviate street congestion.

items.title: Spring Cleanup and Community Announcements
items.summary: Approved a request to schedule a city-wide spring cleanup day and shared announcements regarding upcoming Little League tryouts and a local road race for charity.
